name: Cargo Manifest
description: Goods typing and supply-and-demand pricing laid over physical capacity. It owns the manifest — what goods, how much, bound for which station — and the price quote at each station from local supply and demand curves, because arbitrage between towns is the genre's core read and the quote must come from one place or every station tells a different story. Physical capacity stays in inventory.core_inventory: a hold or wagon is a bag with a manifest attached, and full means full for the same reasons everywhere else in the library, which is why this component listens to inventory.itemAdded and inventory.itemRemoved instead of re-counting. Payment on delivery goes through economy.currency, keeping the money trail auditable. It deliberately does not own spoilage, contraband legality, or passenger comfort — goods here are honest freight, and each of those is a modifier another component can layer on.

inputs.name: goodsCatalog
inputs.description: Goods definitions: id, unit weight, base price, perishability class. Authored content; the component supplies pricing behavior, not the goods themselves.

inputs.name: priceElasticity
inputs.description: How strongly delivered supply depresses local price. High elasticity punishes dumping a full train on one town; low elasticity flattens the arbitrage game away.

inputs.name: demandRefreshSeconds
inputs.description: How often station demand recomputes. Demand that shifts mid-delivery feels rigged; demand that never shifts removes timing from the trade.

outputs.name: manifestWeight
outputs.description: Total loaded weight. Vehicle range and speed penalties read this rather than re-walking the manifest.

outputs.name: manifestValue
outputs.description: Current quoted value of the load at its destination, the number that makes a route feel worth defending.
